pushback_verification: Every finding was re-read against the REDESIGNED state rather than the reviewed state, because the mechanism changed between the pass and the walk. Six dissolved — the slot's gate-scoping defect, the false non-leak proof, the epitome's second read, the missing table row, the write-path pointer, and the unimplementable absence-grep were all defects in a per-site suppression mechanism the redesign abandoned. Dissolution is recorded as RESOLVED with the reason, never silently dropped, and each entry states what replaced the thing the finding was about. TWO findings SURVIVED the redesign and are the reason the new shape is not simply smaller: the system-mode diff carries the partner's committed emit by construction (the handoff preflight guarantees a clean, pushed tree), and the launching brief has no artifact behind it. Both are now requirement clauses with tasks. THIS WALK ALSO FALSIFIED ITS OWN EVIDENCE BASE: Case 4 claimed that under external-first the orchestrator 'holds nothing to leak at the moment it dispatches the fresh half'. That is false — the external findings land BEFORE the fresh half is dispatched, so the orchestrator holds them, and the brief is its own context rather than a file, so neither ordering nor the diff exclusion reaches it. The case was corrected in place with a note on how a wrong claim survived an enumeration that was otherwise correct: it was written in the same sitting. Catching it here rather than in a third pass is the only reason it is not a third-iteration CRITICAL. Also recorded as an open question: bare `/orbit:address-reviews` is defined as a whole-repo marker scan with no auto-discovery anchor, so with zero markers and exactly one active change carrying two unwalked passes, its defined behaviour is a clean no-findings exit; this walk proceeded by judgment.

resolutions.title: `next_hint_keys.slot` is not gate-scoped: while the tracked `apply` gate is `ready`, the field carries no slot at all, so a system-mode blind pair run in that window is never blinded
resolutions.action: DISSOLVED BY REDESIGN (D-rc03a-9/10/11, ratified before this walk). The finding is correct and is one of the two reasons the slot was abandoned as a signal. Nothing reads `next_hint_keys.slot` under the ordering mechanism; the gate-scoping defect is recorded in design.md D3 so it is not rediscovered as available.
resolutions.resolution: Dissolved by the redesign ratified before this walk (option A: ordering plus one exclusion).

resolutions.title: The non-leak proof is false: with the pair empty and a prior pass unwalked, the slot is ABSENT and the pair's first member runs with context retained
resolutions.action: DISSOLVED BY REDESIGN (D-rc03a-9/10/11, ratified before this walk). Correct, and the second reason the slot was abandoned: the empty-pair branch sits downstream of the resolution clause, so `pair empty` does not imply `slot rendered`. No proof is required under ordering — the mechanism does not reason about slot presence. Recorded in design.md D3.
resolutions.resolution: Dissolved by the redesign ratified before this walk (option A: ordering plus one exclusion).

resolutions.title: The internal branch has a SECOND prior-findings read — the disciplines epitome — and task 2.7 protects the sentence that orders it
resolutions.action: DISSOLVED BY REDESIGN (D-rc03a-9/10/11, ratified before this walk). The epitome's pushback comparison matches `review-<mode>-*.json`, and under external-first the partner's findings are `external-<as>-*.md`, which that glob cannot match. The channel is EMPTY rather than suppressed, so no task guards it and task 2.3 states explicitly that no prior-run-read edit is made anywhere.
resolutions.resolution: Dissolved by the redesign ratified before this walk (option A: ordering plus one exclusion).

resolutions.title: The fresh half's blindness is delivered by the launching brief, which no requirement or task constrains
resolutions.action: SURVIVES THE REDESIGN and is now a first-class requirement clause plus task 2.2: a dispatched blind-pair member's brief carries the change name, mode and pass set only, naming no finding, count, severity or trend. This walk ALSO found that Case 4's claim that ordering retires this channel was FALSE — under external-first the orchestrator holds the external findings when it dispatches the fresh half — and corrected the case in place rather than leaving it for a third pass. design.md D2 and the Risks section both state that no artifact check can enforce it.

resolutions.title: System mode's `git diff <change-start>..HEAD` carries the partner's committed emit — and the external handoff's preflight forces it to be committed first
resolutions.action: SURVIVES THE REDESIGN as the one residual ordering does not empty, and is now a requirement clause plus task 2.1: the blind path's commit range excludes the change's own `.orbit-runs/`, in both places the instruction appears. The finding's causal chain — files committed, preflight requires clean-and-pushed, therefore inside the range by construction — is carried into the requirement verbatim.

final_assessment: 15 findings walked against a change whose mechanism was redesigned between the pass and the walk. 14 resolved, 1 deferred. Six dissolved — they were defects in a suppression mechanism that no longer exists — and the two that SURVIVED the redesign became first-class requirement clauses: the system-mode diff exclusion and the launching-brief constraint. The walk also found and corrected a false claim in its own evidence base: Case 4 asserted ordering retires the launching-brief channel, and it does not.
